sourceList.title: Ervin’s Take ★
sourceList.desc: Overall picture: provisional blended polling averages (RCP 40%, DDHQ 29%, 270toWin 21%, Silver Bulletin 10%). Silver is intentionally downweighted because its comparable historical Senate-polling backlog is limited. Distinct named publisher averages remain eligible even when the same page cites them; proxy filtering and freshness safeguards remain; Original Ervin correction is the default; Michigan also has a discounted, unvalidated candidate-primary overpolling adjustment in Ervin’s Take; Ervin + remains an option.

historical.kind: GOP campaign-sponsored Cygnal Oct 14–16 final-round RCV poll
historical.notes: Candidate-matched 2024 Peltola vs Nick Begich. Poll predicted Peltola 47.9–52.1 (D−4.2); certified final RCV 48.78–51.22 (D−2.44). One Republican-associated poll; both comparisons use final RCV round. Survey commissioned on behalf of Begich and NRCC; downweighted as partisan in evidence-weighted variant.
Context only, not part of Peltola-specific correction: October Alaska Survey Research Harris 43, Trump 51.
Candidate-matched 2022 Peltola vs Sarah Palin November general election: modeled final runoff 53–47 (D+6); certified final RCV 54.96–45.04 (D+9.92). Survey precedes election by several weeks.

2020 Senate polling of incumbent Dan Sullivan (R) against Al Gross (independent/D-aligned); Sullivan is the same Republican incumbent running against Peltola in 2026. Relevant opponent continuity and office, but 2020 predates ranked-choice general elections in Alaska. Included in evidence-weighted correction with a 0.60 continuity multiplier.

states.notes: Candidate-specific correction uses Peltola's 2022 general and 2024 House ranked-choice final-round polling errors; older 2020 Senate and 2024 presidential comparisons remain audit context for Original Ervin; they contribute to Ervin +. Both Peltola comparisons involve different Republican opponents and the 2022 survey predates election day by several weeks. 2026 Senate polls reported as 2-candidate or first-round margins may not be comparable to final RCV runoff results; interpret adjusted margins as a sensitivity scenario, not an estimated final-round outcome. Evidence-weighted setting also includes Sullivan's 2020 Senate polling error at 0.60 same-Republican-incumbent multiplier and the 2024 statewide presidential error at 0.35; Peltola's own House comparisons retain 1.35; the 2020 Senate election features incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan, who is again on the ballot in 2026. Same-year entries share weight.
